title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: New, untested driver; no past data; plausible but uncertain; noise-adjusted uplift shrunk to x1.15 from prior trend effects

drivers.name: Price increase
drivers.evidence: Price up 4.5% from $9.88; last similar price week saw no lift (96 units vs baseline 96.5); likely dampens demand

adjustment.analysis: Thanksgiving week historically shows a slight dip (x0.94 vs baseline, noise-adjusted x1.0), so no adjustment. The price increase to $10.32 (+4.5%) is above recent levels (last $10.32 week: 96 units, baseline 96.5) and no prior lift observed at this price. However, TikTok trend is a new, untested driver with no historical precedent. The classical model suggests no uplift, but the trend could drive demand. Given thin evidence and high noise, shrink effect toward 1.0. No promotion, so no post-promo dip. Final adjustment is conservative.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.5 | 5%-95%: 62.5 - 234.1 | 10%-90%: 67.1 - 191.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
